issues.rule_name: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

issues.title: Inconsistent date filter causes missing bookings in recurring event cancellation
issues.description: When cancelling recurring bookings with 'allRemainingBookings' flag, the code updates bookings using 'new Date()' as the time threshold but then fetches updated bookings using 'bookingToDelete.startTime'. This creates a time window mismatch where bookings between these two timestamps will be cancelled in the database but won't be included in 'allUpdatedBookings', causing workflow reminders and calendar event cleanup to be skipped for those bookings. This leads to orphaned reminders and stale calendar events that were cancelled but never properly cleaned up.

issues.title: Missing return value breaks caller's count tracking
issues.description: The 'updateMany' method in BookingRepository no longer returns the Prisma update result object which contains the count of updated records. According to the IBookingRepository interface, this method should return 'Promise<{ count: number }>', but the implementation now returns 'Promise<void>'. This breaks any calling code that depends on knowing how many bookings were updated, potentially affecting audit logging, metrics, or conditional logic that needs to verify if the update affected any records.

issues.title: Missing locale field causes translation failure in cancellation flow
issues.description: The 'userSelect' object used by UserRepository.findById (and subsequently findByIdOrThrow) no longer includes the 'locale' field. However, in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code calls 'getTranslation(organizer.locale ?? "en", "common")' which expects the locale property on the organizer object. Since locale is now undefined, the translation will always fall back to 'en' regardless of the user's actual locale preference, causing cancellation emails and notifications to be sent in the wrong language for non-English users.

issues.title: Repository files violate naming convention using dot-suffix pattern
issues.description: Three new repository files in apps/api/v2 use dot-suffix naming pattern (.repository.ts) which violates Rule #1 of the compliance rules. The rule explicitly prohibits dot-suffixes like '.repository.ts' and requires PascalCase filenames matching class names (e.g., PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository.ts). This affects code discoverability, consistency, and violates the established architectural standards documented in AGENTS.md. The files should be renamed to match the PascalCase pattern used throughout the rest of the codebase.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #24159 - chore: [Booking Cancellation Refactor - 2] Inject repositories and use them instead of Prisma in cancellation flow
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the booking cancellation flow in `handleCancelBooking.ts` off direct Prisma calls and onto injected repositories (`UserRepository`, `BookingRepository`, `ProfileRepository`, `BookingReferenceRepository`, and a new `PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository`). It adds DI modules for the new repositories, wires them into `BookingCancelService`, and adds thin API v2 adapter classes. It also adds three recurring/seated/reference cancellation tests and fixes a duplicate `onBookingCancelled` call, which I confirmed is now a single call.

The direction is sound and the DI wiring follows the existing module pattern. However, I found one build-breaking defect and several behavior regressions. Two DI module files import paths that do not exist in the repo, so the DI graph will not compile or load. `userSelect` lost `locale` while the cancellation flow still reads `organizer.locale`, so organizer-facing notifications silently fall back to English. The recurring-cancellation query now filters from the cancelled booking's `startTime` instead of `now`, which pulls past, non-cancelled instances into the post-cancel cleanup loop. The new tests only assert `success` and `bookingId`, so none of these regressions would be caught.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The DI modules reference paths that do not exist (`@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference`, `@calcom/prisma/prisma.module`), so the change does not compile or load. That alone blocks merge. The dropped `locale` silently changes organizer-facing language, the widened recurring `gte` runs post-cancel side effects on instances that were never cancelled, and `BookingRepository.updateMany` does not satisfy its interface. The new tests do not catch any of these. All of these are small, targeted fixes.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `BookingCancelService` (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts) took a single `prismaClient` dependency and the `handler` function called `prisma.user`, `prisma.profile`, `prisma.booking`, `prisma.attendee`, and `prisma.bookingReference` directly. Callers reach the service either through the DI container (`BookingCancelService.module.ts`) or through the API v2 Nest module (`apps/api/v2/src/lib/modules/booking-cancel.module.ts`), which re-exports platform-library classes via `packages/platform/libraries/repositories.ts`.

This PR replaces those direct calls with five repository dependencies. Each has its own DI module under `packages/features/bookings/di/` or `packages/features/users/di/`, and the API v2 layer provides Nest-injectable subclasses that receive `PrismaWriteService.prisma`. The `handler` accepts an optional `Dependencies` object. When it is absent, the handler constructs repositories from the global `prisma` import, so the default `handleCancelBooking` export keeps working. The PR also adds new query methods on `BookingRepository` and `ProfileRepository` that mirror the original Prisma selects, and a new `updateManyByBookingId` on `BookingReferenceRepository`.
steps: Entry points: `BookingCancelService.cancel` (handleCancelBooking.ts) is reached either from the DI container or from the API v2 Nest module. It now forwards `this.deps` into `handler` instead of dropping them.

Dependency wiring: `BookingCancelService.module.ts` binds five repositories by token. The new `BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts` and `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` plus `Profile.module.ts` are the new DI modules. Those three import paths are where the build breaks.

Organizer and profile lookups: `handler` now calls `userRepository.findByIdOrThrow` and `profileRepository.findFirstByUserId`. The user select dropped `locale`, so downstream `organizer.locale` reads are affected.

Recurring cancellation: `updateMany` and `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` run for `allRemainingBookings` or `cancelSubsequentBookings`. The post-cancel loop then deletes workflow reminders and webhook triggers for every returned booking.

Single-booking path: attendee deletion goes through `PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository`, the booking is updated through `updateIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` keyed on `uid`, and reference soft-delete goes through `updateManyByBookingId`.

findings.title: DI modules import paths that do not exist in the repo
findings.body:
Two new DI module files import from paths that are not in the repository, so the DI graph cannot compile or load.

- `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` imports `BookingReferenceRepository` from `@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference`. That path does not exist. The class actually lives at `@calcom/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository`, which is the file this PR edits and the one `handleCancelBooking.ts` imports.
- All three new module files import `moduleLoader as prismaModuleLoader` from `@calcom/prisma/prisma.module`. That file does not exist under `packages/prisma/`. The existing Prisma loader is `packages/features/di/modules/Prisma.ts`, which `BookingCancelService.module.ts` already used before this PR.

Because `BookingCancelService.module.ts` imports `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts`, loading the cancel-service module fails, and the TypeScript build reports unresolved modules.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/di/BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts" lines="1-4"}

::callout{type="warning"}
The same unresolvable `@calcom/prisma/prisma.module` import also appears in `BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts` (line 4) and `packages/features/users/di/Profile.module.ts` (line 4). Fixing only the first file will not be enough.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` (lines 3-4), the imports are wrong. Change the `BookingReferenceRepository` import to `@calcom/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository`, which is the class the cancel flow actually uses. Change the `prismaModuleLoader` import to `@calcom/features/di/modules/Prisma`, matching the pattern in `BookingCancelService.module.ts`. Apply the same Prisma-loader fix to `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts` (line 4) and `packages/features/users/di/Profile.module.ts` (line 4). Then verify that `BookingCancelService.module.ts` loads without unresolved imports.

findings.title: organizer locale dropped from user select, so organizer notifications fall back to English
findings.body:
The PR removes `locale: true` from `userSelect` in `UserRepository.ts`. `findByIdOrThrow` calls `findById`, which selects with `userSelect`, so `organizer.locale` is now always `undefined`.

The cancellation flow still reads it in two places: `getTranslation(organizer.locale ?? "en", "common")` and the `language: { locale: organizer.locale ?? "en" }` payload for the organizer calendar event. Before this PR the organizer's locale was honored. After it, every organizer-facing cancellation email and calendar description is silently rendered in English, with no error.

This is a silent behavior change, which is the kind the PR says it must not introduce. The fix is to restore `locale: true` in `userSelect`. Other callers of `UserRepository` that pick up `locale` via separate selects (for example lines 351 and 1120) are unaffected, but `findById` is not.

::diff{file="packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts" lines="99-102"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts`, the `userSelect` constant (around lines 83-125) no longer includes `locale: true`, which was removed between `completedOnboarding` and `timeFormat` (around lines 100-101). `findById` uses this select, and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` reads `organizer.locale` at about lines 337 and 370. Restore `locale: true` in `userSelect`. Do not change the other selects. Then add a test that asserts `organizer.locale` is populated after `findByIdOrThrow`, so this regression is caught.

findings.title: Recurring cancel filter widened from now to booking startTime, cleaning up non-cancelled instances
findings.body:
In the recurring branch, the `findMany` that feeds `updatedBookings` changed its `startTime` filter. The original query used `gte: new Date()`. The new one uses `gte: bookingToDelete.startTime`.

When `allRemainingBookings` is true and `cancelSubsequentBookings` is false, the `updateMany` above cancels only instances with `startTime >= now`. The `findMany` now returns every instance with `startTime >= bookingToDelete.startTime`, which includes past instances that were never cancelled. The loop after it then:

- deletes scheduled webhook triggers and no-show tasks for those past bookings,
- deletes their workflow reminders through `WorkflowRepository.deleteAllWorkflowReminders`,
- passes them to `onBulkBookingsCancelled`, which emits cancellation audit and webhook events for bookings that did not change.

The new tests do not catch this because they assert only `success`.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts" lines="513-518"}

::callout{type="warning"}
The PR description lists this as a high-risk area, but the conditional `now`/`startTime` choice was not carried over. Keep the original `new Date()` semantics for the `findMany` and leave the `updateMany` as it is.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-cancellation `findMany` (around lines 513-518) filters with `gte: bookingToDelete.startTime`. The original code used `gte: new Date()`, and this PR changed it without a reason. That pulls past, non-cancelled instances into `updatedBookings`, which then deletes their webhook triggers and workflow reminders and emits cancellation events for them. Restore the filter to match the `updateMany` semantics above it: use `new Date()` when `cancelSubsequentBookings` is false and `bookingToDelete.startTime` when it is true, or simply restore `new Date()` to match the original. Add a test where a past instance of a recurring event exists and assert it is not cancelled or emitted.

findings.title: BookingRepository.updateMany return type does not satisfy IBookingRepository
findings.body:
`BookingRepository` declares `implements IBookingRepository`. The interface declares `updateMany(...): Promise<{ count: number }>`, but the new implementation returns `Promise<void>` because it discards the Prisma result.

TypeScript rejects this under `implements` (TS2416, incompatible return type), which breaks type-checking for the package. It also means callers cannot read the affected count, which the interface promised.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts" lines="1502-1507"}

The same method's indentation is also off by one level, which the formatter would flag.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts`, `updateMany` (around lines 1502-1507) returns `Promise<void>`, but `IBookingRepository` in `packages/lib/server/repository/dto/IBookingRepository.ts` declares `Promise<{ count: number }>`. Make the implementation `return await this.prismaClient.booking.updateMany({ where, data });` so it returns Prisma's `{ count }`, which satisfies the interface. Also fix the method's indentation to match the surrounding methods. Do not change the interface unless a caller needs a different shape.

findings.title: New tests assert only success and bookingId, so they cannot detect the regressions in this PR
findings.body:
The three new tests in `handleCancelBooking.test.ts` have the same assertion block: `success` is true, `onlyRemovedAttendee` is false, and `bookingId` equals the input. None of them check the behavior this refactor is meant to preserve.

- The seated test never checks that attendees were deleted, even though the test name says "delete all attendees".
- The recurring tests never check which instances were cancelled, so the widened `gte` above passes unnoticed.
- The "booking reference cleanup" test seeds two references with `deleted: null` and never checks that they were soft-deleted, so the `updateManyByBookingId` path is not covered.
- Nothing exercises the injected-dependency path. The tests call the default export, which takes the fallback branch in `handler`.

A test that asserts `result.success` would pass even if the attendee or reference deletion were removed. These tests give false confidence about the refactor.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts" lines="1513-1515"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts`, the three tests added near the end of the file (seated event around line 1056, recurring around line 1163, subsequent around line 1284, and reference cleanup around line 1405) assert only `success`, `onlyRemovedAttendee`, and `bookingId`. Extend them to assert the behavior their names describe: the seated test should verify the attendee rows are gone, the recurring tests should verify which instances are now CANCELLED and that past instances are untouched, and the reference test should verify the references are marked `deleted: true`. Use the existing scenario helpers' DB assertions in the same file. Also add one case that asserts `organizer.locale` reaches the email payload, to catch the dropped-locale regression.

findings.title: Fallback construction path is live and duplicates the DI wiring
findings.body:
`handler` takes an optional `dependencies` argument. When it is missing, it builds all five repositories from the global `prisma` import. The `BookingCancelService` path always passes `this.deps`, but the default `handleCancelBooking` export does not, so the fallback is live. The tests use that export, which means the DI path is not covered by them.

This leaves two construction sites that must stay in sync. The PR says the dual paths must match, but nothing enforces it, and they already diverge: the fallback constructs `new PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository(prismaClient)` directly, while the DI module binds it through a separate module.

The PR description calls this "backward compatibility during transition". A cleaner option is to make the default export build deps once with the same factory the DI module uses, so there is a single wiring point.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts" lines="139-155"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handler` (lines 139-155) builds a fallback set of five repositories from the global `prisma` when `dependencies` is not passed. `BookingCancelService` always passes its deps, but the default `handleCancelBooking` export does not, so that path is live and duplicates the DI wiring. Replace the inline fallback with one shared factory that the DI module and the default export both call, so there is a single construction point. Keep the `Dependencies` shape unchanged. Make sure the default export still works without a DI container.

findings.title: New attendee repository file uses different quote and semicolon style
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/repositories/PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository.ts`, the imports and class use single quotes and no semicolons, unlike the rest of the package. Reformat the file with the repo formatter so it uses double quotes and semicolons, matching `BookingRepository.ts` and `UserRepository.ts`. No logic change.

findings.title: Single onBookingCancelled call after the duplicate fix
findings.body: The PR description says a duplicate `bookingEventHandlerService.onBookingCancelled()` call was removed during merge resolution. I checked the head: there is now exactly one `onBookingCancelled` call, in the single-booking branch, and the recurring branch uses `onBulkBookingsCancelled`. That fix is correct.

findings.title: Simplified uid-based where clause is safe
findings.body: The original code used `uid ? { uid } : { id }` for the single-booking update. The PR now always keys on `bookingToDelete.uid`. This is safe because `Booking.uid` is declared `@unique` in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and `bookingToDelete` has already been loaded by the time this runs, so its `uid` is always present. This removes a branch without changing which row is updated.

findings.title: Repository injection follows the existing DI module pattern
findings.body:
The new DI modules use the same `createModule` / `bindModuleToClassOnToken` / `moduleLoader` shape as the existing modules, and the new tokens are added alongside their peers in `tokens.ts`. The API v2 subclasses are thin: they only forward `PrismaWriteService.prisma` to the platform-library base class, and the base classes are exported through `packages/platform/libraries/repositories.ts`. That keeps the API layer from duplicating query code.

One caveat: the services' `Dependencies` type names `PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository` from the features package. Keep that type and the API v2 export in sync when either side changes.
